# Privacy allowlist (see scripts/privacy_scan.py --allow).
# One regular expression per line, optional whitespace-separated "# reason" suffix.
# A '#' that is not whitespace-separated is part of the pattern, not a comment.
#
# Each entry is one fully escaped, anchored literal: no class, no wildcard, no
# alternation. A new secret is fixed at source and never added here. Each entry is
# one quoted value that cannot be reworded after it is committed: two path families
# (the pi install tree and the operator user name - D-20261019-CEO-8,
# D-20261019-CEO-15) and four fabricated values quoted as evidence: three probe
# values (D-20261020-CEO-4) and one example path (D-20261031-CEO-2). The file itself
# is the list; nothing here counts it.
#
# What an entry exempts is the text the scanner matched, not a directory: a finding
# is exempt when its matched text matches any pattern here. For `home-path` and
# `agent-config` that text is the rule's own match - the home prefix, or the config
# directory - never the rest of the path. So `^\.pi/agent/npm$` covers every
# `agent-config` finding whose value is that install tree, and `^/home/pingz$`
# covers every `home-path` finding for that home path - whether the path ends
# there, at `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, or anywhere else under it, because the text after the
# match is not part of the value. A credential rule is unaffected by either entry:
# a token, key or password on the same line is still reported, and a sibling user
# name does not match.
#
# This file is self-exempting, and that is the one thing to remember about it: the
# entries are patterns, so the file itself matches the literals it lists and is
# only clean when it is passed as its own `--allow`. Every change here is therefore
# a security change - justify the entry in the same commit and have it reviewed as
# one, never to make a run green.

# ^\.pi/agent/npm$ - opened by T-0001. It exempts one host install prefix that is
# quoted twice: the scanner's own fixture at tests/unit/test_privacy_scan.py (the
# tree), and a pre-fix blob of references/Adapters.md with the audit quotations of
# it (history), so `--tree` and `--history` are both red without it. What the tree
# no longer carries is any reference to the package that path once held (T-0038):
# no shipped surface, package manifest or fixture names it. Rewriting that
# unpublished history would invalidate commit SHAs quoted as evidence in
# docs/Team/Archive.md and docs/Team/Decisions.md.
# Nothing from package-lock.json is blessed: the scanner does not report its
# "resolved" tarball URLs.
^\.pi/agent/npm$

# ^/home/pingz$ - the operator user name, which appears as a build path in one
# archived reviewer finding and in the justification text of this file. The
# exemption is fixed by SHAPE (one literal user name), never by count: the number
# of historical blobs that quote it grows with every commit that documents it.
# A user name is not a credential, which is why this shape - and nothing else - is
# exempted; anything secret on such a line is still caught by its own rule.
^/home/pingz$

# ^C:\\Users\\Ping$ - the same operator user name on the Windows host, opened by
# T-0018 under D-20261101-CEO-3 (ceo T-0011), which amends D-20261019-CEO-8/-15
# and AuditReport F-P1 rather than being re-argued here: that ruling assumed the
# source fix was cheap, and it is not - a PowerShell variable expanded into an
# absolute path inside the --result line of two commit messages (e4b046f, 5b63723)
# that are ancestors of main with 44 commits and 40 cited SHAs above them, and
# --reflog keeps the old messages reportable after any rewrite. The exemption is
# fixed by SHAPE (this one user name under the Windows user directory), never by
# count: neither line carries a credential, a sibling user name, the forward-slash
# form of the same path and every credential rule stay armed, and the control is
# committed in tests/unit/test_privacy_scan.py. The cause is fixed at source as
# well - a --result line is single-quoted, so no shell variable expands into a
# home path.
^C:\\Users\\Ping$

# The three fabricated probe values below are what a reviewer's own evidence
# quoted while proving that the gate CATCHES a credential; they are not secrets,
# they were invented to be caught. They reached docs/Team/Archive.md through the
# verbatim quote and now live in two blob revisions of unpublished commits, so
# the choice is the same one D-20261019-CEO-15 records: exempt the exact literal
# instead of rewriting history and invalidating the SHAs the archive cites.
# Each entry is anchored and fully escaped, so any other token, passphrase or
# password shape on the same line is still reported.
^sk-live-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef$
^hunter2 passphrase$
^changeme-placeholder$

# ^C:/Users/x$ and ^C:/Users/x\.py$ - a fabricated example path, opened by
# D-20261031-CEO-2. The superseded Architecture.md section-13 example read this
# path while the merged section reads the C:/temp form, and the archive quotes the
# old value while explaining the red - a quotation that cannot be reworded after
# it is committed. No account is named: the "user" segment is the file name x.py.
# Two entries because the rule reports what follows the user name: the full
# C:/Users/x.py where the value ends there, and the bare C:/Users/x where a
# backslash follows it - this file's own entry line is the second case, because an
# escaped dot puts a \ after the name.
^C:/Users/x$
^C:/Users/x\.py$
# ^ping\.zhao@nidvue\.com$ - the operator's own identity, opened by
# D-20261110-CEO-8. The operator directed that every commit be authored as
# "Ping Zhao <ping.zhao@nidvue.com>" and that the identity be the team's preset
# author, so the address is a committed constant (src/teamwork/config.py) and the
# author of every commit above the published tip. It is the operator's identity,
# not a secret: it is published by this commit and by every release author field.
# A credential rule is unaffected - this exempts one literal address, nothing else.
^ping\.zhao@nidvue\.com$
